about: A remixed Zork: white house, kitchen, living room with lantern and sword, trap door to a cellar, with the troll moved right next to the cellar.

done.why: I died to the troll, which sits one room from the start of the underground, and was dumped in a forest with my items gone. Starting over for the same fight didn't appeal.

ending.what: Died to the troll and was respawned in the forest.

moments.note: The troll is immediately north of the cellar, much earlier than I expected.
The fight is mostly luck. I got knocked out and disarmed and had no way to read the odds or retreat.
Died and landed in the forest with no explanation of what I lost.
The sword and lantern are both easy to grab, and the sword glows near danger.
'take leaflet and read it' was rejected as 'can't see any such thing'.

wished: A way to flee or avoid the troll
A warning before the fight that I was underpowered

lines.line: Your sword has begun to glow very brightly.
lines.why: A good warning of danger, and it hints the world is playing fair.

lines.line: The troll's axe stroke cleaves you from the nave to the chops.
lines.why: Vivid death line, but it ended my short session.

fun.why: The opening was pleasant, then I died fast in a fight I couldn't read.

engagement.why: I wanted to explore, but the troll blocked me almost at once and I lost interest after dying.

difficulty.why: A hard troll fight with no preparation, one room into the dungeon.

interestingness.why: Familiar Zork with the troll moved. That's a neat twist but I barely saw more.

prose.why: Classic, clean prose; the combat lines are colorful.
